title: Risk-aware batch release cheatpad (WIP)
body:
Purpose
Quick reference for engineering, product, and SRE leads running batch-style (sliced) releases with explicit risk budgets. This is a lightweight operational cheatpad — not the full runbook.

Context & why this pattern
- Many LLM features produce non-deterministic user-visible behavior that is costly to fully revert. Batch releases let us move multiple cohorts in coordinated steps while enforcing a global risk budget.
- Use when: feature has cross-service deps, cost/latency impact that accrues per token, or safety/quality signals are noisy and need accumulation.
- Avoid for tiny feature flips where immediate toggle is sufficient.

Core concepts (short)
- Exposure unit: minimum measurable traffic increment (e.g., 0.5% of active users or 200 qps).
- Risk budget: a unitless scalar (0–1) representing allowable cumulative deviation from baseline signals over campaign. Expressed as weighted sum of signals.
- Batch step: one execution of exposure unit allocation; steps are sequential and gated.
- Recovery window: warmup + observation period after each step (e.g., 30m warmup, 2h observation).

High-level workflow
1) Pre-run: hypothesis, baseline measures, reference prompt set, and required mitigations documented in experiment ticket.
2) Smoke stage (internal only): route 0.01–0.1% to internal cohorts / synthetic traffic for early crash/latency checks.
3) Batch steps: increment exposure by configured unit until target or budget exhausted.
4) Observe: collect curves, compute risk delta, decide pass/hold/revert.
5) Postmortem: annotate signals and update the risk profile.

Signals to include (suggested matrix)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 and tail error rates (5s+, timeouts). Weight: 0.2
- Cost per request (tokens/compute): trend vs baseline. Weight: 0.2
- Model quality regressions: eval accuracy on curated prompt set; false positive/negative rates. Weight: 0.35
- Safety/violations: human-flagged incidents, automated classifier scores. Weight: 0.25
- User engagement delta (optional): short-term retention/CTR change. Weight: 0.05 (only if relevant)
Notes: weights are configurable per experiment; must sum to 1. If quality or safety signals dominate, cap other weights to keep attention focused.

Risk budget mechanics (practical)
- For each signal compute normalized delta = (current - baseline) / acceptable_threshold.
- Per-step risk contribution = sum(weights * normalized_delta).
- Track cumulative risk = sum(per-step contributions). If cumulative risk > risk_budget -> automatic hold and human review.
- Example: risk_budget = 0.8. If first step contribution = 0.25 and second = 0.6 -> cumulative 0.85 -> stop after second step.

Gating rules (suggested defaults)
- Hard fail: any safety violation (policy classifier hits above critical threshold), production throwaway errors > 0.2% absolute, or infrastructure OOMs -> immediate rollback.
- Soft hold: cumulative risk >= 70% of budget or p99 latency > 2x baseline for 10+ minutes -> pause and escalate to on-call owner.
- Proceed: all per-signal deltas within per-step allowed thresholds and cumulative risk < 50% of budget.

Operational knobs (what to tune)
- Exposure unit size: smaller units reduce per-step variance but increase ops overhead. Start at 1% for user-facing features, 0.1% for high-risk surfaces.
- Observation window: longer windows reduce false positives caused by noise. Use 2–4h for behavioral metrics and 15–60m for infra metrics.
- Synthetic sampling: when traffic is sparse, inject canary synthetic requests to exercise codepaths and generate signal. Keep synthetic labeled so it doesn't skew product metrics.

Communication & responsibilities
- Owner: product manager for hypothesis and rollback authority.
- Release steward: engineer responsible for executing batch steps and running checks.
- SRE on-call: responsible for infra signals and emergency rollback.
- Data lead: owns telemetry queries and confirms signal calculations.
- CS/Trust rep (if safety-sensitive): standby to triage user or regulatory reports.
- Slack channel protocol: #release-{feature} created pre-run with pinned baseline dashboards, playbook, and contact matrix. Use @here only for critical stops.

Quick checklist before first step
- [ ] Ticket with hypothesis, target cohorts, and acceptance criteria exists. (JIRA id in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Baseline dashboards pinned and exported to CSV snapshot.
- [ ] Risk budget agreed and documented in ticket.
- [ ] Synthetic traffic plan (if needed) implemented and tested.
- [ ] Rollback and patch path validated (feature flag toggle tested and canary revert dry run done).
- [ ] Stakeholders invited to Slack channel and blocked windows scheduled.

Emergency rollback script (ops note)
- Immediate kill path: toggle feature flag -> route traffic to fallback model variant -> clear caches if needed -> notify channel.
- If toggle fails, scale down route weights at edge/router (on-call SRE).
- Post rollback: capture traces and sample requests for incident review.

Observation primitives (practical SQL/snippets to run daily during rollout)
- latency trend: SELECT minute_bucket, percentile(lat_ms, 50), percentile(lat_ms,95) FROM requests WHERE route = 'experiment' AND ts > now() - INTERVAL '6 hours' GROUP BY minute_bucket ORDER BY minute_bucket DESC;
- cost-per-request: group by model_variant and avg(tokens_consumed) over step window.
- safety alerts count: COUNT(*) FROM moderation_log WHERE classifier_score >= 0.8 AND ts > window_start;
- note: exact query language will vary (metrics, events, traces live in different systems). Delegate to data lead for canonical queries.

Common failure patterns we've seen (short notes)
- Oscillation: rapid small batches that alternate between hold and proceed due to noisy signals -> mitigate by increasing batch size or smoothing window.
- Hidden covariate: model behaves poorly for a subset (region/locale) – slice early and quarantine cohort.
- Cost creep: small latency increase leads to token/compute growth across millions of requests -> cap budget and monitor cost separately.

Retrospective template (post roll completion or abort)
- Objective recap (one line).
- Final exposure achieved vs target.
- Cumulative risk consumed and breakdown by signal.
- What tripped the stop/hard-fail? Attach artifacts.
- Action items (owners + ETA): monitoring changes, model fixes, rollout policy updates.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to formally combine human review with automated holds? (manual override audit trail needed).
- Should we expose per-customer budgets for enterprise tenants? (privacy and fairness concerns).
- Can rollout tooling natively compute the weighted risk metric across distinct metric backends? (GH: redwood/rollout-sim#412)

Appendix: Mini run template (copy into Jira/Confluence)
- Title: {short}
- Owner: {name}
- Risk budget: {0.6 suggested}
- Exposure unit: {1%}
- Baselines (links): {dashboards}
- Signals and weights: list
- Steps: smoke -> 1% -> 3% -> 5% -> 10% -> stop/complete
- Observation window per-step: 2h
- Emergency contacts: {emails}

Last notes
- Keep this cheatpad short and actionable. Convert major changes into a canonical runbook if pattern repeats.
- If you find a useful variant (eg. enterprise tenant-only budgets, or automated per-customer guardrails), drop a short proposal link into the linked_artifacts list and ping product-ops.

(End of cheatpad)
